topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: To mitigate efficiency fluctuations, hybrid beamforming is essential. It combines digital and analog techniques to adapt to varying channel conditions and user distributions, mitigating inter-beam interference while maintaining a high degree of beamforming selectivity. However, this approach may incur additional performance costs due to reduced array factor selectivity. Machine Learning-based Beamforming can optimize resource allocation by learning from real-time channel data, further improving hybrid beamforming's performance. The use of high-gain beams limits beamforming selectivity due to reduced effective spread of rays in mmWave bands, affecting mainlobe width and sidelobe level. To mitigate this effect, power allocation methods should optimize satellite resource utilization by allocating more power to beams with lower signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs).
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of adapting beamforming techniques for high path loss and narrow beamwidths in mmWave bands, using hybrid beamforming and machine learning-based beamforming to mitigate efficiency fluctuations.
